claims: The Artemis II crew returned to Earth on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II crew had a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
8:07 p.m. EDT is equivalent to 5:07 p.m. PDT.
The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
The Artemis II mission was the first crewed flight to orbit the Moon in over 50 years.
The Artemis II entry interface occurred at 7:53 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II splashdown time was 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II splashdown location was the Pacific Ocean west of San Diego.
The recovery ship for Artemis II was USS John P. Murtha.
The Artemis II crew members are NASA's Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA's Jeremy Hansen.
The four Artemis II crew members were reported to be in good health following their journey.
